mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an active monetary easing policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending confidence and corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE increases by >0.5pp over 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate broad-based demand contraction that triggers reduced corporate revenue expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both RSAFS and HOUST decline for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 (INDPRO < 100) indicates supply chain disruption that increases input costs and compresses corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Annualized CPIAUCSL exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.5% annually, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and rises in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate dual supply-labor market shocks that reduce corporate profitability and trigger negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening regimes (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) intensifies recession risk and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.
